title: Adaptive GPU Quota Stewardship and Backpressure for Recoverable Degradation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We see intermittent OOM cascades during peak mix workloads (long-context chat + concurrent embeddings) that are not well-handled by current eviction-first logic. This ticket implements an adaptive GPU quota stewardship layer that: (1) maintains soft per-model/per-tenant GPU quotas derived from historical usage, (2) applies admission-time backpressure with token-level degradation proposals, and (3) orchestrates coordinated retries and a predictable client-facing degradation mode instead of token-level crashes. Goals are to reduce P99 OOMs, make degradations predictable, and provide richer observability for rollback and postmortem analysis.

Problem statement and motivation:
- Root cause: sudden spike in long-sequence requests exhausts KV + activation memory concurrently, triggering OOMs that cause node restarts or hard request failures.
- Existing mitigations (aggressive eviction, model fallback) are reactive and cause jitter or high latency; they also produce noisy retries that amplify load.
- Customers see hard errors on production LLM routes with mixed request shapes. We need a graceful, predictable flow that prioritizes availability and bounded correctness loss.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Quota Steward: a lightweight, in-runtime tenant/model quota oracle that maintains a sliding-window estimate of GPU working-set (KV + activation) per request type. Not a hard allocator — applies soft quotas and emissions for admission controller.
2) Admission Controller Enhancements: When soft quota would be exceeded, the admission controller can choose among: (a) apply micro-degradation (reduce max_generated_tokens / reduce decode beam / request fidelity flag), (b) schedule a short backoff (100-500ms) and retry with warm KV, or (c) route to a lower-memory variant model. Policy selection is guided by per-route SLOs and per-tenant degradation budget.
3) Progressive Degradation Plan: Define a deterministic degradation ladder per model: TOKEN_TRIM -> REDUCED_KV_PREFETCH -> DOWNSHIFT_TO_QUANT_MODEL -> ROUTE_TO_SMALLER_MODEL. Each step has an estimated memory delta and expected quality loss.
4) Spill & Resume: If activation memory would overflow, attempt a controlled spill of cold KV shards to host memory (best-effort, bounded to X ms additional latency) and resume. Track spill success/failure in spans.
5) Retry Choreography: Retries must be idempotent and observable; attach a retry_token in tracing and cap retries to avoid thundering-herd amplification.
6) Observability & SLOs: Add per-tenant metrics for steward decisions, degradation events, spill latency, and retry frequency. Surface a new console chart "Quota Steward Decisions" for operators.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Benefit: avoids hard OOMs by choosing predictable degradation strategies and centralizing decision logic.
- Trade-off: slightly more complex admission path and additional per-request bookkeeping (microseconds). We accept minimal CPU/metadata overhead in exchange for fewer node restarts and better customer UX.
- Consistency: soft quotas are eventually consistent across workers. For tight cluster capacity cases we will rely on conservative lower bounds and cross-worker signals (heartbeat summary).
- Fallback model strategy: prefer quantized variants on the same node family when available to reduce memory copy costs.

Progress updates:
- 2025-09-10 (Maya Chen): Drafted ticket and prototype algorithm for sliding-window working-set estimator. Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Quota+Steward+Design+v1.
- 2025-09-12 (Ethan Rodriguez): Initial runtime hooks added for tracking per-request KV + activation peaks. Benchmarked added overhead ~40us/request on p4d instance. Benchmark notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/steer/benchmarks/quota-steward.
- 2025-09-14 (Ethan Rodriguez): Implemented micro-degradation API (degradation_hint in request metadata) and a simple policy engine that decides TOKEN_TRIM vs retry. Unit tests added (admission_policy_test). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1893 (WIP).
- 2025-09-16 (Design review by Priya Nair): Feedback: make degradation ladder configurable per-tenant and add a "user-visible" field in API indicating degradation level for analytics. Action: add tenant config and API opt-in toggle.
- 2025-09-18 (SRE sync): SRE requested an emergency circuit-breaker that flips to "reject with 429 + explanation" when cluster-level memory pressure exceeds 95% for >30s. Added dependency on cluster-pressure metric stream (ENG-42784).

Open questions and decisions needed:
- How to compute tenant quotas for bursty, low-history tenants? Proposal: start with a conservative default and allow tenants to opt-in to aggressive stewardship via account config.
- Should we expose degradation hints to end-customers via the API? PM lean: yes, but opt-in and only as a structured header.
- Spill policy SLA: bound host-memory spill latency to 250ms for interactive routes; need performance validation.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for steward estimator and policy decisions.
- Integration test simulating mixed workload shapes with synthetic KV/activation footprints at varying concurrency.
- Canary: roll to a single dedicated pool used by internal dev org with traffic shaping. Monitor SLOs (P50/P95 latency, P99 error rate, OOM count).
- Gradual ramp and kill-switch: runtime flag to disable stewardship and prefer eviction-first behavior.

Metrics to watch (new):
- steward.decision.{token_trim,retry,downshift,spill,route_small}
- steward.spill.latency_ms
- steward.retry.count and steward.retry.success_rate
- node.oom.count (target: -90% in canary)
- route.degradation_rate and route.user_visible_degradation_pct

Backward compatibility and API notes:
- Add optional request metadata field "degradation_hint" and response header "X-Degradation-Level". These are opt-in; default behavior unchanged until steward is enabled for a route.

Next actions (owner assignments):
- Ethan: finish retry token plumbing, add cap logic, and implement circuit-breaker hook (ETA 2025-09-22).
- Maya: update design doc with tenant opt-in API and degradation telemetry mapping (ETA 2025-09-20).
- SRE (Tom Alvarez): wire cluster-pressure metric to steward hook and validate 95% threshold logic (ETA 2025-09-24).
- QA: prepare integration harness to replay production traces for mixed workloads (owner: Lin Park).

Acceptance criteria (for Done):
- Steward can be toggled per-route and makes decisions according to policy.
- Canary shows >80% reduction in hard OOMs for canary traffic and no more than 5% increase in P95 latency.
- Observability surfaced in console with event counts and traces annotated with decision metadata.
- Docs updated and at least one customer engaged in early access.

Notes on uniqueness vs existing tickets:
This ticket focuses on a central decision layer ("Quota Steward") and admission-time backpressure with a deterministic degradation ladder and retry choreography. It intentionally moves away from purely eviction-first approaches and from ad-hoc model swaps into a policy-driven, observable stewardship flow intended to improve predictability for customers while minimizing node-level restarts.
